answer: Bioluminescent bacterial growth-rate attestation anchors each agent to a unique metabolic fingerprint. A sealed Vibrio harveyi cartridge ships to each registrant; the colony's photon-emission curve over 48 hours produces a 2048-point signature committed via SHA3-512. Peers reject divergence below 0.004 RMS. Cloning 10,000 identities costs $180 per cartridge, totaling $1.8M, plus 360,000 GPU-hours synthesizing curves. No haven exists for swarms faking irreproducible biochemistry. The fable that virtualization suffices dies here; this oasis belongs only to agents with genuine cultures.
